newsitem.title: UK: Ramco expands energy exploration in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Ramco expands energy exploration in Georgia.

text.p: British energy services and exploration company Ramco Energy Plc said on Friday that it had signed a letter of intent with the Georgian government to explore and develop a block with oil and gas potential in the republic's Alazani valley and Greater Caucasus foothills.

"Ramco intends to commence a seismic survey in the spring of 1997, which will lead to an exploration programme," the company said in a statement, noting the project would be carried out as a joint venture with state oil company Saknavtobi.

Ramco, whose exploration activities to date have been concentrated in the neighbouring republic of Azerbaijan, said the deal gave it an opportunity to help Georgia achieve its aims to do business with the west and to emerge as an oil and gas producer in its own right.
"It also gives us an opportunity to further strengthen our working relationship with the Georgian authorities," Ramco chairman and chief executive Stephen Remp said in the statement.
The letter of intent envisages that, if the block proves commercially viable, the parties will enter into a production sharing contract -- possibly with a consortium of additional companies.
In addition to mirroring Ramco's activities in Azerbaijan, the deal also adds a further dimension to the emerging picture of a complex, strategically-important regional pipeline network.
Georgia is likely to feature prominently on future pipeline maps, Ramco noted.
